_comment: G-8: every display string in the game, English only in MVP. Keys are ui_<screen>_<element> or n_<event>_title/_body (doc 08's event ids). Full table is authored alongside the screens; the entries below fix the conventions and the load-bearing templates.
_plural_rule: A template may carry a <key>_one variant, used when its count argument is exactly 1 (English needs two forms; 0 and 2+ take the base key, so the base is written in the plural). The count is the template s only numeric placeholder; a template with several names its selector in a sibling <key>_plural entry. UIConfig.t() applies this; tests/test_ui_strings.gd holds the file to it.
_source: docs/design/12-ui-ux.md §3.1 + §8. Placeholders are {named} only — never positional %s. Lookup is Str.t(key, args). A missing key returns the key itself in a debug build and is a test failure (doc 12 test 21).

ui_level_2_intent: Houses pay tax. Shops pay more, and give the people in the houses somewhere to work.

ui_level_3_intent: Every building you own costs money every hour, and the street outside it costs money once. Decide what the city charges.

ui_level_4_intent: Something will fail. Have somebody standing by before it does.
ui_level_4_teaches: Teaches: stations and coverage, the incident drawer, keeping what you own in repair, and holding a city together for a full day.
ui_level_5_intent: You have run out of ground and you are drinking somebody else's water. Buy the first and build the second.
ui_level_5_teaches: Teaches: buying land, the development pipeline, and your first water works.
ui_level_6_intent: The ground is full and the ladder is not. Put a tower on land you already own, and take one building all the way to the top of it.
